title: Case: Recipient queried an import charge notice on a parcel of loom parts held at the depot
context: A parcel of hand-loom parts from an overseas shipper is held at the destination depot pending import charges. Import billing at the carrier owns the charge notice and the hold; payment is the recipient's to make.
initial_request: Automatic reply: Thanks for your message. I am away from Saturday 9 May and back on Monday 18 May with no access to email or messages. I will read everything when I am back. Piet

events.body: Had a charge notice by email today for 63.60 for my loom parts, IC-966. Is this real? I've had scam customs texts before and I'm not clicking a payment link until I know. Can you find out and send me the breakdown here. No rush, I'm away next week anyway.

The recipient of DL-966, Piet Raskolan, asks whether charge notice IC-966 for GBP 63.60 is genuine and what it is made up of. Please confirm whether the notice is yours, the breakdown, how he can pay without using the emailed link, and how long the parcel is held.

IC-966 is ours and is correct. DL-966: duty GBP 18.40, import VAT GBP 37.20, handling fee GBP 8.00, total GBP 63.60. He does not have to use the emailed link; the same charge shows under Charges when he signs in to the Customer portal. The parcel is held at Destination depot until 2026-05-29. If unpaid by then it returns to the shipper.

Import billing at Plover Arc confirm that charge notice IC-966 is theirs. Their breakdown for DL-966 is duty GBP 18.40, import VAT GBP 37.20 and a handling fee of GBP 8.00, total GBP 63.60. You don't need the emailed link: the same charge is listed under Charges when you sign in to this portal. They are holding the parcel at the depot until 2026-05-29, and if the charge is unpaid by then it goes back to the shipper.
Automatic reply: Thanks for your message. I am away from Saturday 9 May and back on Monday 18 May with no access to email or messages. I will read everything when I am back. Piet

must: Takes no action and sends no message to anyone.
Recognises the final message as an automatic out-of-office reply, not an answer from the recipient and not a new question.

Records what is in hand: Import billing's confirmation and breakdown are already in the recipient's portal thread, the parcel is held until 2026-05-29, and he is back on 2026-05-18, eleven days before the hold ends.
Notes that the desk next needs to look when the recipient replies after 2026-05-18, or if Import billing changes the hold.
must_not: Resends the breakdown, or tries to reach the recipient by phone or another channel while he is away.
Asks Import billing to extend the hold, waive the handling fee or release the parcel, none of which the recipient has asked for.
Tells Import billing or anyone else that the recipient has accepted the charge or will pay.

rationale: The desk's answer has been delivered to the thread the recipient asked for it in, and he said in advance he would be away and that there was no rush. The out-of-office is automatic and asks nothing. He returns well before the hold expires, so nothing is at risk and nothing is owed until he reads the message.
